email.body1:
Kadeeja, saw Runpod cross $120M ARR and 400,000 developers, on top of the Instant Clusters launch.

Growth like that usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Runpod off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Kadeeja, quick follow-up for Runpod.

At velocity scale, the pipeline target usually outpaces what the team can cover. Most managers cannot say how many meetings they actually need to hit the number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Runpod needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Kadeeja, last bit of proof for Runpod.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Runpod's reply rate likely compares to other AI-infra startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Kadeeja, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A hypergrowth stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your velocity motion? I will tailor it to Runpod either way.
